name: Albania
alt: A world map with a small highlighted country along a sea coast in the southeast of a continent, mountains rising right behind its shore.
facts: It's scattered with hundreds of thousands of concrete bunkers built decades ago by a paranoid government bracing for an invasion that never came.
Its flag features a two-headed eagle, and its old nickname translates to 'Land of the Eagles.'
Many of its rivers and lakes are so clean and blue they look almost tropical, despite being tucked into rugged mountains.

name: Austria
alt: A world map with a landlocked highlighted country in the middle of a continent, draped across a long mountain range.
facts: It's home to the oldest zoo in the world still operating today, founded inside the grounds of an old imperial palace.
One of its cities was home to so many history-changing composers that it's often called the world's classical music capital.
More than half of it is covered by a single sweeping mountain range that draws skiers from all over the world.

name: Belarus
alt: A world map with a landlocked highlighted country in the middle of a continent's eastern half, covered largely in flat forest and farmland.
facts: It's landlocked, with no coastline touching any sea.
One of its ancient forests is one of the last places in Europe where wild bison still roam, much as they did centuries ago.
It uses a language closely related to two of its neighbors, written in the same alphabet as one of them.

name: Belgium
alt: A world map with a small highlighted country squeezed between several larger neighbors near a continent's northwestern coast.
facts: It's home to the headquarters of a major international alliance and a union spanning much of its continent.
It has three official languages, and many road signs switch between them depending on where you are.
Despite the name people often give them, the crispy fried potato strips known as 'French fries' likely got their start here.

name: Bosnia and Herzegovina
alt: A world map with a highlighted country in the middle of a mountainous peninsula, with just a tiny sliver of coastline reaching a sea.
facts: A single gunshot fired in its capital in 1914 helped trigger a war that pulled in countries across the globe.
One of its old stone bridges was rebuilt brick by brick after being destroyed in a war in the 1990s, using the same building methods as centuries ago.
Its capital once hosted the Winter Olympics, filling its surrounding mountains with the world's best skiers.

name: Bulgaria
alt: A world map with a highlighted country along the eastern edge of a peninsula, bordering a sea and tucked beneath a mountain range.
facts: Archaeologists found what's considered the oldest worked gold in the world buried in a cemetery here, dating back thousands of years before the pyramids.
Its valleys grow so many roses that a huge share of the world's rose oil, used in perfumes, comes from here.
Many people here nod their head for 'no' and shake it for 'yes' — the opposite of what visitors expect.

name: Croatia
alt: A world map with a highlighted country shaped like a crescent, curving along a sea coast dotted with countless small islands.
facts: Its coastline is scattered with more than a thousand islands along a sparkling sea.
A walled medieval city here became famous worldwide after a hit fantasy show used its streets as a filming location.
The neckwear we now call a 'necktie' is believed to have started here, inspired by scarves worn by soldiers centuries ago.

name: Czechia
alt: A world map with a landlocked highlighted country in the middle of a continent, surrounded by hills on nearly every side.
facts: People here drink more beer per person than anywhere else in the world.
Its capital is home to an astronomical clock from the 1400s that still keeps working centuries later.
It's famous for a sparkling type of glass that's been crafted here for hundreds of years.

name: Denmark
alt: A world map with a small highlighted peninsula and cluster of islands at the northern edge of a continent, reaching up between two seas.
facts: A small wooden toy company here invented the colorful interlocking bricks that kids all over the world now snap together.
In its capital, there are more bicycles than people, with wide lanes built just for them.
It's regularly ranked among the happiest countries on Earth.

name: Estonia
alt: A world map with a small highlighted country along the northeastern edge of a continent, facing a sea dotted with islands.
facts: It was one of the first countries in the world to let people vote online in national elections.
A popular video-calling app used by millions worldwide was first built by engineers here.
Its capital's old town is so well preserved that walking through it feels like stepping into the Middle Ages.

name: Finland
alt: A world map with a highlighted country stretching far up toward the Arctic, covered in thousands of lakes and dense forest.
facts: It has more saunas than people, tucked into nearly every home and apartment building.
It's been ranked the happiest country in the world several years in a row.
Above its Arctic Circle line, the sun doesn't set at all for weeks during summer.

name: France
alt: A world map with a highlighted country shaped roughly like a hexagon, spanning the western edge of a continent between two seas.
facts: It's the most visited country on Earth, welcoming tens of millions of tourists every year.
Deep in one of its caves, people thousands of years ago painted animals on the walls that still survive today.
An iron tower built for a world's fair here was originally meant to be torn down after just 20 years.

name: Germany
alt: A world map with a highlighted country in the middle of a continent, bordered by many other countries on almost every side.
facts: Stretches of one of its major highways have no speed limit at all.
A man here built the first printing press with movable metal type, changing how information spread across the world forever.
One of its festivals draws millions of visitors every year to celebrate with huge tents, music, and traditional food.

name: Greece
alt: A world map with a highlighted country at the southern tip of a peninsula, fragmented into a mainland plus a scatter of many islands.
facts: It's where the very first Olympic Games were held, thousands of years ago.
It has thousands of islands scattered across its surrounding seas, though only a couple hundred have anyone living on them.
Many ancient stories said its tallest mountain was home to a family of powerful gods.

name: Hungary
alt: A world map with a landlocked highlighted country in the middle of a continent, shaped roughly like an oval.
facts: A professor here invented a colorful twisting puzzle cube that's sold hundreds of millions of copies worldwide.
Its capital is built over natural hot springs, and bathing in steaming open-air pools is a beloved pastime.
Its underground train system was the first of its kind anywhere on its continent outside of one other city.

name: Iceland
alt: A world map with a small highlighted island alone in the middle of a cold northern ocean, far from any other landmass.
facts: Almost all of its electricity and heating comes from volcanoes and hot springs bubbling beneath the ground.
It's one of the only places on Earth with no mosquitoes at all.
Its language has changed so little over a thousand years that people here can still read ancient sagas without much trouble.

name: Ireland
alt: A world map with a highlighted island just west of a much larger neighboring island, both off the northwestern coast of a continent.
facts: A holiday celebrating its patron saint is celebrated with parades and green clothing in cities all over the world, even where hardly anyone has ties to it.
One of its oldest illustrated books, covered in intricate hand-drawn designs, was created by monks more than a thousand years ago.
Its rugged western coast drops off in towering cliffs that plunge hundreds of feet straight into the ocean.

name: Italy
alt: A world map with a highlighted country shaped like a tall boot kicking a small island, stretching down into the middle of a sea.
facts: It has more UNESCO World Heritage Sites than any other country on Earth.
An entire independent country, the smallest one in the world, sits inside the borders of just one of its cities.
The leaning tower in one of its towns has been tilting for centuries and still hasn't fallen over.

name: Latvia
alt: A world map with a small highlighted country along the northeastern edge of a continent, facing a sea between two neighboring countries.
facts: Its capital has one of the largest collections of a curling, nature-inspired architecture style found anywhere in the world.
Its beaches along the sea are famous for a golden, fossilized tree resin that washes up after storms.
Every few years it holds a massive song and dance festival where tens of thousands of performers take the stage together.

name: Lithuania
alt: A world map with a small highlighted country along the northeastern edge of a continent, with a short stretch of coastline on a sea.
facts: A monument near its capital marks what's been calculated as the geographic center of its entire continent.
Basketball is such a national obsession here that winning international tournaments can feel like the most important thing happening in the country.
It's known for having some of the fastest average internet speeds anywhere in the world.

name: Luxembourg
alt: A world map with a tiny highlighted country squeezed between three much larger neighbors near the middle of a continent.
facts: It was the first country in the world to make all of its public buses, trams, and trains completely free to ride.
Most people who grow up here learn to speak three or more languages fluently.
It's one of the smallest countries on its entire continent, yet has one of the highest average incomes in the world.

name: Moldova
alt: A world map with a small, landlocked highlighted country tucked between two larger neighbors in the eastern part of a continent.
facts: It's landlocked, with no coastline touching any sea.
One underground wine cellar here is so enormous, with so many miles of tunnels, that it holds the record for the largest collection of wine bottles on Earth.
It's one of the least-visited countries on its continent, despite all that wine.

name: Montenegro
alt: A world map with a tiny highlighted country along a dramatic, mountainous stretch of coastline on a sea.
facts: Its name translates to 'Black Mountain,' after the dark, looming peaks that rise near its coast.
A dramatic bay along its coastline is lined with steep cliffs and medieval walled towns, often compared to a fjord.
It's one of the smallest countries on its continent by population.

name: Netherlands
alt: A world map with a small, low-lying highlighted country along a continent's northwestern coast, laced with canals and reclaimed land.
facts: About a third of its land sits below sea level, protected by an enormous system of dikes and pumps.
It has more bicycles than people, and cyclists often outnumber cars on its streets.
Each spring, vast fields here burst into color with rows of a flower that's become one of its biggest exports.

name: North Macedonia
alt: A world map with a small, landlocked highlighted country on a mountainous peninsula, tucked between several neighbors.
facts: It's landlocked, with no coastline touching any sea.
One of its lakes is among the oldest lakes on Earth, with some species of fish and snails found nowhere else.
It changed its own name in recent years after a long-running dispute with a neighboring country over a shared historical name.

name: Norway
alt: A world map with a long, jagged highlighted country running up the western edge of a peninsula, its coastline cut by deep inlets.
facts: Its coastline is carved into deep, dramatic fjords left behind by ancient glaciers.
It's home to one of the longest road tunnels in the world, stretching for miles through solid rock.
Glowing green and purple lights often dance across its night skies during winter, far north of the equator.

name: Poland
alt: A world map with a highlighted country along the northern part of a continent, with a short coastline on a sea and flat plains stretching inland.
facts: An ancient forest along its eastern border is one of the last places in Europe where wild bison still roam free.
An astronomer born here helped prove that the planets circle the sun rather than the other way around.
Many of its cities were rebuilt brick by brick after being heavily damaged in a war, using old paintings and photos as guides.

name: Portugal
alt: A world map with a highlighted country along the western edge of a peninsula, facing a vast ocean.
facts: It has some of the oldest unchanged borders of any country in the world, dating back centuries.
It produces more cork than any other country on Earth, harvested from the bark of trees without cutting them down.
Centuries ago, sailors from here set off on voyages that helped connect Europe with Africa, Asia, and the Americas for the first time.

name: Romania
alt: A world map with a highlighted country in the southeastern part of a continent, wrapped around a curving mountain range.
facts: A region here inspired the legend of a famous fictional vampire, drawing tourists to its castles ever since.
Its forested mountains are home to one of the largest brown bear populations left in Europe.
One of its rivers fans out into a vast wetland delta before reaching the sea, teeming with rare birds.

name: Russia
alt: A world map with an enormous highlighted landmass stretching across the entire northern half of two continents at once.
facts: It's the largest country on Earth by far, spanning eleven time zones from one end to the other.
One of its lakes is the deepest and oldest freshwater lake in the world, holding about a fifth of all the unfrozen fresh water on the planet.
A single railway line here stretches for thousands of miles, connecting one side of its vast territory to the other.

name: Serbia
alt: A world map with a landlocked highlighted country in the middle of a mountainous peninsula.
facts: It's landlocked, with no coastline touching any sea.
More than a dozen ancient Roman emperors were born in towns and cities within its borders.
It's one of the world's biggest exporters of a small red berry used in jams, desserts, and yogurt everywhere.

name: Slovakia
alt: A world map with a small, landlocked highlighted country in the middle of a continent, its northern border lined with jagged peaks.
facts: It's landlocked, with no coastline touching any sea.
It has more castles per person than almost any other country in the world.
Its northern border is lined with jagged, snow-capped peaks that look almost alpine despite belonging to a smaller mountain range.

name: Slovenia
alt: A world map with a small highlighted country tucked at the head of a sea, between mountains and a tiny strip of coastline.
facts: More than half of its land is covered by forest, one of the highest shares anywhere in Europe.
A tiny church sits on an island in the middle of one of its alpine lakes, reachable only by traditional wooden boats.
It was one of the first countries in the world to be officially certified as a sustainable 'green' destination for travelers.

name: Spain
alt: A world map with a highlighted country covering most of a peninsula in the southwest of a continent, facing both an ocean and a sea.
facts: It has more bars and cafes per person than almost any other country in the world.
Every summer, crowds run alongside bulls through narrow streets in one of its most famous festivals.
A fiery, passionate dance style performed with quick footwork and clapping has its roots in one of its southern regions.

name: Sweden
alt: A world map with a long highlighted country running down a peninsula's eastern side, facing a sea across from several neighbors.
facts: The prizes considered the most prestigious in science, literature, and peace were created using the fortune of an inventor born here.
A law here gives everyone the right to walk, camp, and forage on almost any land, even land they don't own.
A furniture company founded here in a small village grew into one of the largest furniture retailers on the planet.

name: Switzerland
alt: A world map with a small, landlocked highlighted country in the middle of a continent, draped across a tall mountain range.
facts: It has stayed officially neutral in wars for more than two centuries.
Deep underground near its border with a neighboring country, scientists smash tiny particles together at nearly the speed of light to study what the universe is made of.
It's one of the largest consumers of chocolate per person in the world.

name: Ukraine
alt: A world map with a large highlighted country in the eastern part of a continent, with a coastline on a sea in the south.
facts: It's the largest country whose entire territory lies within its continent.
Its rich black soil makes it one of the biggest wheat and sunflower oil producers on Earth.
One of its nuclear power plants was the site of the worst nuclear accident in history, back in 1986.

name: United Kingdom
alt: A world map with a highlighted set of islands off the northwestern coast of a continent, separated from the mainland by a narrow sea.
facts: It's made up of four different nations joined together under one flag.
The modern rules for the world's most popular sport were written down here in the 1800s.
It's often considered the birthplace of the Industrial Revolution, when machines first began replacing hand-powered work on a massive scale.
